buyer_budget_summary: CLAIM 1a (July 2026 dermocosmetics buyer, PNG + technical info): VERIFIED. 99Freelas #768972, 18 Jul 2026. The buyer is a dermocosmetics STORE (reseller) buying marketplace/social product videos. The budget is undisclosed ('Aberto', R$50 minimum). There were 9 proposals and it was awarded, price private, with a 2-video paid test. CLAIM 1b (August 2026 brief preserving packaging, logo, text, colors and geometry): NOT FOUND for any beauty or cosmetics buyer, so UNVERIFIED as stated. Sources checked: 99Freelas projects 763000-787500 (26 Jun to 25 Sep 2026; 17.077 live pages, 6.727 fetched in full by title filter) and Workana open listings on 33 queries. Fidelity clauses are COMMON in cheap non-beauty AI product briefs in Jul-Sep 2026: toys (#776283/#776351, 14-15 Aug), fashion (#771869), bags (#781340, 208 proposals, 'fidelidade ao produto físico deve ser 100%'), product swap (#784613), Mercado Livre (#766504). Also one perfume brand on Workana (24 Sep, 'preservando a autenticidade dos produtos'). Fidelity is a table-stakes requirement at the R$50-500 tier, not a premium signal. DISTRIBUTION OF WHAT BUYERS SAY THEY WILL PAY: every beauty/cosmetics visual-production post with a stated budget is between < USD 50 and USD 500 per PROJECT, i.e. about < R$259 up to R$2.590. The single highest is 30 AI videos for USD 250-500 (R$43-86 per video). Beauty AI-video or launch-film posts: < USD 50 (x3), USD 50-100 (x2), USD 250-500 (x1). The only beauty budget above USD 500 is USD 500-1.000 for BRANDING a new kids' line, not campaign visuals. On 99Freelas the buyer never states a budget: 6.702 of 6.727 fetched projects are 'Aberto' with a R$30-100 platform minimum, and offers are private. So 99Freelas proves the demand exists and says nothing about price. ZERO observed buyer posts at or near the plan's R$2.990 for a one-product set. The one launch-film buyer (a new Brazilian K-beauty brand, 11 Sep) budgets USD 50-100 for post-production. Coverage limits: 99Freelas covers Jul-Sep 2026 only, not 2025. Workana shows only OPEN jobs (closed ones are unsearchable, and the insight pages are 'Access Denied'). GetNinjas, Fiverr requests and LinkedIn were not searched.

preview_test.method: TA_CONSULTA_COSMETICOS.CSV (dados.anvisa.gov.br, downloaded today). Hair/skin keyword filter on rows with DT_VENCIMENTO 2036-07-27..2036-09-25, i.e. notified 2026-07-27..2026-09-23. That gives 4.929 rows from 792 holders. A random sample of 15 distinct holders (seed 20260925) was checked for a public packshot on the brand site, marketplaces and web search. Instagram could not be read: r.jina.ai returned 'Anonymous access to domain www.instagram.com blocked', and direct fetches hit a login wall. Mercado Livre served an account-verification wall. A secondary ICP sample of 6 established brands was checked the same way.
preview_test.key_finding: All 3 exact packshots are RE-NOTIFICATIONS of products already on sale (Derma Fine 2017 notification, Keune 2023, Affirm 2007/2015), so none of them is a launch. Among the 12 genuinely new SKUs: 0 exact packshots, 3 sibling-only, 9 nothing public. The ICP sample of established brands (n=6) shows the same pattern: 3 exact, all re-notifications (Natura Faces, Neutrogena Hydro Boost, and Adcos, a RENAMED re-notification of its 2019 'STICK FPS UVB 80 PEACH'); 2 sibling-only (Wella Ultimate Hydra, a new line beside Ultimate Repair/Smooth; Widi Care Juba new SKU); 1 none (Alia Beauty PDRN). Pooled, 0 of 15 genuinely new SKUs had a public exact packshot when the ANVISA signal fired. 20,8% of all 4.929 recent hair/skin notifications carry a product name identical to an earlier notification (1.026 rows). That is a lower bound on re-notification noise, because renamed ones like Adcos are missed.
preview_test.implication: At the moment the ANVISA signal fires, a watermarked preview of THE launch cannot be built from public material. It can only be built from a sibling's packshot with the new label invented, which is the exact fidelity failure the plan's 'Product Lock' forbids, or not at all (10/15). Where a public packshot does exist, the 'launch' is usually a re-notification of an on-sale product, so there is nothing to launch. Fix options: (a) trigger on the brand's own public 'em breve'/launch post instead of ANVISA (later, but the pack exists); (b) use ANVISA only to FIND brands, and build the preview from the brand's CURRENT hero product; (c) ask for the die-line/artwork, which is unreleased client IP (see higgsfield_training).

higgsfield_training.terms_version: Last updated July 26, 2026; effective immediately for users registering on/after 26 Jul 2026, on 27 Aug 2026 for earlier users
higgsfield_training.clause_4_4: "You acknowledge and agree that Your Content, Inputs, and Outputs may be used by Company to train, develop, enhance, evolve, and improve its (and its affiliates’) AI models... Different terms apply to enterprise and business customers who use the Service under an Enterprise Agreement (see Section 1.3); under those agreements, Company does not use the customer's content to train or improve its AI models, and that content is handled as confidential. ... You can stop this going forward by deleting Your Content or your Account"
higgsfield_training.clause_4_2: User represents 'you have all necessary rights to Your Content to grant the licenses set forth in Sections 4.3 and 4.4' and that it does not infringe third-party trademark/copyright
higgsfield_training.clause_16_5: Deletion does not reach '(iii) content already used to develop or improve Company's AI models before deletion, which cannot feasibly be disassociated from models already trained'
higgsfield_training.privacy_2_3: 'using your user-shared multimedia data, query and prompt data, and Inputs and Outputs ... to train and improve our (and our affiliates') AI models'. Also shares with 'third-party AI model and compute providers'
higgsfield_training.opt_out: NONE on self-serve (Free/Plus/Ultra; the team-plan page https://higgsfield.ai/team-plan states no no-training term). The only stop is deleting the content or account, which is prospective only. The arbitration clause has an opt-out; training does not.
higgsfield_training.enterprise_no_training: YES, contractual. https://higgsfield.ai/enterprise: 'Does Higgsfield train AI models on our data? No. Higgsfield Enterprise never trains models on your data... contractual no-train guarantee... built for unreleased products, embargoed campaigns, and confidential client material.' Price: 'credit-based pricing on annual contracts with monthly payments, sized to your team's seats' (no public price, 'Contact Sales'), so it is UNVERIFIED and very likely outside C5.
higgsfield_training.answer: YES. On a self-serve plan, uploading a client's unreleased packaging artwork as an Input licenses Higgsfield (and affiliates) to train on it, and Sol warrants she holds the rights to grant that licence. A client NDA or confidentiality clause is breached by construction. Only an Enterprise Agreement (annual, sales-gated, unpriced) removes this.

google_gemini_api_paid.url: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms (read via r.jina.ai; direct fetch hits an OAuth redirect loop)
google_gemini_api_paid.quote: "When you use Paid Services, including, for example, the paid quota of the Gemini API, Google doesn't use your prompts (including associated system instructions, cached content, and files such as images, videos, or documents) or responses to improve our products"
google_gemini_api_paid.caveat: Unpaid Services (AI Studio free, free quota) DO use content: 'Do not submit sensitive, confidential, or personal information to the Unpaid Services.' This matters because Higgsfield's own product-photoshoot recipe runs nano_banana_pro, a Gemini image model. The same model through a billed Gemini API project is under a no-train contract.

corrections_to_plan: July 2026 dermocosmetics buyer EXISTS (99Freelas #768972, 18 Jul 2026), but it is a reseller STORE buying marketplace videos (Mercado Livre/Shopee/TikTok Shop), budget undisclosed ('Aberto', R$50 minimum), awarded after a 2-video paid test. It is evidence of the cheap marketplace-content tier, not of a R$2.990 launch buyer.

The 'August 2026 brief preserving packaging, logo, text, colors and geometry' was NOT FOUND for any beauty buyer (99Freelas 26 Jun-25 Sep 2026; Workana open listings). Near-identical fidelity clauses appear in toys, fashion, bags and generic product-swap briefs at R$50-minimum 'Aberto' budgets. Packaging fidelity is a commodity REQUIREMENT, not a premium signal.

Observed buyer budgets for beauty visual production run < USD 50 to USD 500 per project (< R$259 to R$2.590). The richest AI brief pays USD 250-500 for 30 videos (R$43-86/video). No beauty buyer post was observed near R$2.990 for a one-product set.

Orne: 'short AI videos around R$29,90-R$85' should read R$29,90-R$89 (10 s model video = R$89). Its 'Fidelidade total ao produto' is a feature bullet, not a guarantee. The plan's full deliverable set prices at about R$280-360 on Orne's list: R$2.990 is 8-11x that.

Villo: the R$19,90 unit is 1 product x 3 variations (~R$6,63/image). Villo ALSO gives a free test image of the client's product, so the free-preview mechanic is already a competitor's front door. Its terms disclaim fidelity ('pequenas variações visuais, textuais ou compositivas podem ocorrer').

Beauty Fair 2026 directory = 491 exhibitors, 229 hair/skin (236 with Barber), categorised, but with NO email or phone (only an Instagram or website link), and it is a post-event 2026 list (next edition 4-7 Sep 2027). It is an annual list of ~229 names, not a trigger.

PREVIEW MECHANIC: at ANVISA-notification time, 0 of 15 genuinely new hair/skin SKUs had a public exact packshot (5 sibling-only, 10 nothing). Every 'exact packshot' case was a re-notification of a product already on sale. At least 20,8% of recent notifications are identical-name re-notifications, and renamed ones such as Adcos are uncounted. So the ANVISA-timed free preview can only be faked from a sibling (a label hallucination, which the Product Lock forbids) or must wait until launch, which forfeits the timing edge.

Higgsfield self-serve (the plan's stack) trains on Inputs with no opt-out. Uploading a client's unreleased packaging artwork licenses it for training and breaks any NDA. No-train needs a Higgsfield Enterprise Agreement (annual, unpriced) or a switch to Adobe Firefly / the paid Gemini API, both of which state no-training in their terms.
